entries.title: Micah 4:1
segments:
vv 1-4. 
 
  But in the last days it shall come to pass; see notes on

. 
 
For the sins of God's ancient people, the literal Zion has long been "trodden down of the Gentiles;" but God has been ever mindful of his spiritual Zion, and he will, at the appointed time, give her dominion over all the earth.

entries.title: Micah 4:3
segments: The prevalence of Christian principles among the nations of the earth will put an end to the custom of war; and this is the only way in which we can hope for its abolition.

entries.title: Micah 4:4
segments: When the fear and love of God shall prevail among all nations, they will enjoy perpetual quiet and prosperity.

entries.title: Micah 4:5
segments: All people will walk--we will walk; while the heathen follow their blind superstitions, we will cleave to our covenant God.

entries.title: Micah 4:6
segments:
Her; Zion, compared to a feeble and scattered flock.  Zion here represents the true church of God from age to age. 
 
vv 6-7. 
 
With God, it is alike easy to abase those who are in high stations for their sins, and to exalt the lowly in spirit.  However depressed may be the condition of his people, if they look to him in penitence and faith, he will grant them a gracious deliverance and enlargement.

entries.title: Micah 4:7
segments: A remnant--a strong nation; a remnant whence shall spring a strong nation.

entries.title: Micah 4:8
segments: Tower of the flock; Zion, the citadel of God's flock,

. 
 
  The first dominion; the supreme dominion,

. 
 
vv 8-10. 
 
Though the history of God's church is one of perpetual conflict, the end shall be redemption from the hand of all her enemies; for "the kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem."

entries.title: Micah 4:9
segments: Why dost thou cry out--is thy counsellor perished? though the dominion shall be given to Zion "in the last days," she must in the mean time pass through a period of humiliation for her sins, without king or counsellor.

entries.title: Micah 4:10
segments: Be in pain; until the coming of the Messiah, Zion is as a woman in travail; that is, she is in a depressed and suffering state, anxiously waiting for her promised Redeemer.  See

. 
 
  Out of the city; out of Jerusalem into captivity. 
 
  Go even to Babylon--be delivered; a remarkable prophecy of the Babylonish captivity, and subsequent deliverance of God's people.

entries.title: Micah 4:11
segments:
Look upon Zion; look with delight upon her humiliation. 
 
vv 11-13. 
 
When God afflicts his people, their enemies rejoice; not understanding that he is thus purifying them from sin, and preparing the way for their triumph over those who hate and persecute them.

entries.title: Micah 4:12
segments: Know not the thoughts of the Lord--he shall gather them; here, as often as elsewhere, God declares that his purpose, in allowing the nations to assemble against Zion, is their own destruction.  Compare

. 
 
  As the sheaves into the floor; the assembled nations are compared to sheaves gathered into the threshing-floor, and Zion is exhorted to arise and thresh them.

entries.title: Micah 4:13
segments: Thy horn--thy hoofs; an allusion to the practice of threshing wheat by driving oxen over it.
